newsitem.title: USA: American to operate extra San Juan freight.
newsitem.headline: American to operate extra San Juan freight.

text.p: American Airlines will make a special freight run between New York and San Juan, Puerto Rico, tonight to relieve a cargo and mail backlog partly attributable to the United Parcel Service strike, AA Cargo vice-president sales Mark Najarian said.
Though the A300 is a passenger aircraft, it will carry only mail and freight, he said. With no passenger luggage aboard, the aircraft will be able to use the entire belly hold for mail and freight.
The flight will leave New York-JFK before midnight and return by early morning to operate its Thursday schedule of passenger flights, he said.
Najarian said the backlog probably reflects several factors, including the UPS strike.
Even without the strike, cargo demand is strong on the San Juan routes, said Najarian.
While American may be moving more cargo and mail throughout its system due to the strike, it has not had to deny space to other cargo customers to accommodate increased mail traffic.
Najarian noted that much of the increase in mail is in parcels, which are less dense than letter traffic. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com cg
